blocks.text: Living in Cypress Park Estates, West Vancouver

Cypress Park Estates, in the District of West Vancouver, is a high hillside community on the Cypress Bowl Road approach to Cypress Provincial Park, well above the Marine Drive villages. It is a recognized upper-slope residential enclave in the District, separate from the British Properties streets farther east. The forested mountain setting is the defining character.

Homes for sale in Cypress Park Estates are mainly houses on large, sloping lots. Cypress Provincial Park and the mountain recreation area sit just up the road. Everyday shops are a drive down to Caulfeild, Dundarave, or Park Royal.

Transit is limited on the upper mountain road, with buses more frequent down on Marine Drive. Nearby public schools include those in the west-side and Cypress-approach families. Check the SD45 school locator. Slope, access, and winter-road conditions should be confirmed with the District.

blocks.text: Condo buildings in Cypress Park Estates

District sources call the existing residential area Cypress Park, Rodgers Creek and the Uplands, and call the planned future neighbourhoods Cypress Village and Cypress West. It's also a different place from Cypress Provincial Park and Cypress Mountain Resort, which are up the same road (Cypress Bowl Road) and aren't residential.
Where Cypress Park Estates sits
Drive time to Cypress Park Estates
Hawksley — 3963 Uplands Way on current MLS listings (District of West Vancouver)

A new condo development by British Pacific Properties with Beedie Living, in the Rodgers Creek and Uplands area. Listings for units at 3963 Uplands Way show concrete freehold strata condos built in 2026, with a fitness centre, residents' lounge, music room, bike workshop and dog wash. Sources disagree on the address (the presale source says 3271–3281 Uplands Way) and the size (57 condos and 7 townhomes in a 10-storey building, a 6-storey building and a townhouse podium, or a 72-unit building). Because it finished in 2026, some units may still be developer sales, with GST and presale rules.
Streets, schools and getting around Cypress Park Estates

items.t: Where the condos are: in one building, Hawksley, on Uplands Way in Rodgers Creek (CD3 zoning). Everything else in the area is detached houses on RS2, RS3 and RS5 streets, semi-detached strata homes, or the future Cypress Village land west of Cypress Bowl Road, where nothing is built yet.

Transit anchor: TransLink route 256 (Whitby Estates / Park Royal), a community shuttle, runs via Chippendale Road to Westhill at the edge of this area, then via 21st Street, Gordon Avenue, 22nd Street and Marine Drive to Park Royal. This is a car-based area.

Nearby: Cypress Falls Park, Cypress Trails Park and Woodburn Park are District parks in the area; West Vancouver Community Centre and Aquatic Centre (2121 Marine Drive) and West Vancouver Memorial Library (1950 Marine Drive) are below in Ambleside; and Cypress Park Primary (IB, K–3) is at 4355 Marine Drive at the foot of the slope. It's named for the area, but check whether it's the catchment school for an address up the hill.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Cypress Park Estates

items.t: District plans and zoning (West Vancouver — its own bylaws): the area sits under the District of West Vancouver Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 4985, 2018, and Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010.

Wildfire and watercourse permits — the defining checks on this slope: a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit is required for work within the Wildfire Hazard Development Permit Area, described as within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface, and the District's Community Wildfire Resiliency Plan describes the Cypress Park area as consistently sloped terrain. An Environmental Development Permit is required for work within 15 metres of the top of any watercourse bank — Cypress Creek and Rodgers Creek both run through the area — and steep-terrain subdivisions can trigger a difficult-terrain permit. These apply to strata alterations and landscaping at Hawksley and Chippendale Mews, not just to house lots.

District tax timing: District of West Vancouver 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on unpaid current taxes on July 2, 2026 and a further 5% on outstanding current taxes on September 2, 2026. District water and sewer utilities are metered and billed quarterly.

blocks.text: Good to know about Cypress Park Estates

items.t: Three Cypress names share one road. The residential pocket, Cypress Provincial Park and Cypress Mountain Resort are different places; a listing that trades on ski-hill proximity is describing a drive up Cypress Bowl Road, not a location inside the resort.

Rodgers Creek just roughly doubled on paper. A District-approved modification of the Rodgers Creek rezoning for Areas 5 and 6 raised the approved homes from 493 across 16 buildings to 974 across 17 buildings, lifted maximum heights from 12 storeys to 14 and up to 16 storeys on some sites, and added two 12-storey buildings with up to 280 purpose-built secured market rental homes combined, with a $7.14 million voluntary community amenity contribution from British Pacific Properties. Hawksley's buyers are buying into the first phase of a much larger build-out.

Cypress Village is approved and its first works are permitted. The Area Development Plan for Cypress Village and Eagleridge was approved by Council with Zoning Amendment Bylaw No. 5206, 2024 creating the Cypress Village (CV) Zone; Development Permit 24-115 to British Pacific Properties Limited covers initial works (commenced January 2025), and the Eagleridge lands transferred to the District (262 acres) were dedicated as park in April 2025. The village's planned shopping, school and community centre are future amenities — do not price them as present.

3900 Cypress Bowl Road falls outside the SD45 locator's listed ranges for Cypress Bowl Road (Even 3850–3850, Odd 3755–3757) — a listing that names a catchment school for an Upper Lands condo is stating something the district's own tool does not confirm.

The area's "primary school" is three grades, at the bottom of the hill. Cypress Park Primary is a K–3 IB PYP school at 4355 Marine Drive whose students have the opportunity to continue the IB programme at West Bay Elementary — it is not a full K–7 neighbourhood elementary for the Uplands, whatever a listing implies.

The new building's own numbers do not agree with each other yet. Hawksley appears as 57 condos + 7 townhomes in its presale source and as a 72-unit development in other project and listing sources, at two different Uplands Way addresses — early-days documentation for a 2026 building is exactly why the strata plan and disclosure/Form B, not marketing pages, govern a purchase here.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Cypress Park Estates

The District calls the area Cypress Park, Rodgers Creek and the Uplands, with Cypress Village and Cypress West planned as future neighbourhoods. It's not the same as Cypress Provincial Park or Cypress Mountain Resort, further up Cypress Bowl Road, which aren't residential. Cypress Park Estates is in the District of West Vancouver, under Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 4985 (2018) and Zoning Bylaw No. 4662 (2010).
Streets, schools and transit near Cypress Park Estates townhomes

items.t: Nearby: Rodgers Creek and the British Properties / Chartwell (east and south-east), Whitby Estates and Westhill (south, below Highway 1), Caulfeild (south-west, across Highway 1), and Cypress Provincial Park / Cypress Mountain (north, up Cypress Bowl Road).

Where the homes are: detached houses on RS2, RS3 and RS5 streets, semi-detached strata homes on Chippendale Road, and one new project with condos and townhouses, Hawksley, on Uplands Way in Rodgers Creek (CD3 zoning). Nothing is built yet on the future Cypress Village land west of Cypress Bowl Road.

West Vancouver is outside SnapStats coverage in Jared's FVR + GVR September 2026 reports — no West Vancouver section, sub-area rows or community medians exist for it, and no other stats source is substituted.

Transit and roads: TransLink route 256 (Whitby Estates / Park Royal), a community shuttle, runs via Chippendale Road to Westhill at the edge of this area, then via 21st Street, Gordon Avenue, 22nd Street and Marine Drive to Park Royal. Cypress Bowl Road is the access road for the residential area and the provincial park; Chippendale Road, Uplands Way and Rodgers Creek Lane serve the residential streets; Highway 1 connects east to North Vancouver and west to Horseshoe Bay. This is a car-based area.

Schools: SD45 catchments are address-based, with elementary (K–7) and secondary (8–12) schools only and no middle tier. Cypress Park Primary (IB PYP), Kindergarten to Grade 3, 4355 Marine Drive, is the school physically named for the Cypress Park area at the foot of the slope — a K–3 primary school, not a full K–7 catchment elementary for an Upper Lands address.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Cypress Park Estates

items.t: For Hawksley (and Chippendale Mews, if title shows it's strata), read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. For a new building like Hawksley, find out first whether the unit is a developer sale (disclosure statement) or a resale (Form B).

Fee simple and bare-land strata: houses on the RS streets are fee simple, but the bare-land strata houses are part of a strata, with a Form B for the strata's shared affairs even though each lot has its own house. The title, not the look of the house, decides.

Plans and zoning: the District of West Vancouver's Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 4985, 2018) and Zoning Bylaw No. 4662 (2010). Zoning here includes the RS2, RS3 and RS5 single-family zones, CD3 for Rodgers Creek (density set by lot size), and the Cypress Village (CV) zone created in 2024. The plan names Cypress Village and Cypress West as future neighbourhoods in the Upper Lands.

Hazard permits — the defining checks on this slope: a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit is required for work within the Wildfire Hazard Development Permit Area, described as within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface, and the District's Community Wildfire Resiliency Plan describes the Cypress Park area as consistently sloped terrain with Cypress Falls Park to the east and the planned Cypress Village west of Cypress Bowl Road. An Environmental Development Permit is required for work within 15 metres of the top of any watercourse bank — Cypress Creek and Rodgers Creek both run through the area — and a subdivision can trigger a difficult-terrain development permit on steep terrain. These apply to strata alterations and landscaping at Hawksley and Chippendale Mews, not just to house lots.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Cypress Park Estates
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Established Upper Lands lots: single-family homes on Chippendale Road, Uplands Way, Woodgreen Drive and the Rodgers Creek streets, in RS2, RS3 and RS5 single-family zones (Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010, Sections 202, 203 and 205), including British Pacific Properties subdivisions of single-family parcels on Uplands Way and at the end of Chippendale Road under the Cypress Village (CV) Zone as the District's development-applications record states them.

Lot character from the zone ladder, as stated: Section 200 minimum site areas are 8,094 m² in RS1, 1,625 m² in RS2, 975 m² in RS3, 731 m² in RS4 and 488 m² in RS5, with RS2 and RS3 the zones named for this area; CD3 (Rodgers Creek) density is set by lot-size band, so a Rodgers Creek lot's size rules come from the CD3 section, not the RS table. These are zone minimums, not a claim about any existing lot's size.
Tenure mix, stated: a genuine mix uphill — freehold detached on the RS streets, strata condos, townhomes and semi-detached homes in the Rodgers Creek CD3 pockets.
Serviced position, as the District states it: West Vancouver water and sewer utilities are metered and billed quarterly by the District.
No ALR percentage split is stated; check any parcel on ALC mapping.

items.t: The Area Development Plan for Cypress Village and Eagleridge was approved by Council, paired with Zoning Amendment Bylaw No. 5206, 2024 creating the Cypress Village (CV) zoning, and the Eagleridge lands transferred to the District were dedicated as park; the District issued Development Permit 24-115 to British Pacific Properties Limited for initial works in the Cypress Village Area, west of Cypress Bowl Road.
Rodgers Creek Area 5 — Development Permit 24-106: Documented here as a permit fact only.

items.t: Nearby areas: Rodgers Creek and the British Properties / Chartwell (east and south-east), Whitby Estates and Westhill (south, below Highway 1), Caulfeild (south-west, across Highway 1), and Cypress Provincial Park / Cypress Mountain (north, up Cypress Bowl Road).

Parks and trails: Cypress Falls Park, with waterfalls, Cypress Creek and off-leash trails, plus Cypress Trails Park and Woodburn Park, are District parks in the area. They're separate from Cypress Provincial Park, home to Cypress Mountain Resort and the Bowen Lookout, Black Mountain Plateau and Hollyburn Peak trails. Recreation: West Vancouver Community Centre and Aquatic Centre (2121 Marine Drive, Ambleside); library: West Vancouver Memorial Library (1950 Marine Drive). Health care: Lions Gate Hospital (231 East 15th Street) and the North Vancouver Urgent and Primary Care Centre (Suite 200, 221 West Esplanade).

Roads and transit: Cypress Bowl Road is the access road for the residential area and for Cypress Provincial Park; Chippendale Road, Uplands Way and Rodgers Creek Lane serve the residential streets; Highway 1 connects east to North Vancouver and the Lions Gate Bridge route to Vancouver and west to Horseshoe Bay and Highway 99. TransLink route 256 (Whitby Estates / Park Royal), a community shuttle, runs via Chippendale Road to Westhill at the edge of this area, then via 21st Street, Gordon Avenue, 22nd Street and Marine Drive to Park Royal.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Cypress Park Estates

parts.t: The rules that apply across Surrey (zoning, suites, strata, land and taxes) are on one page:
buying a home in Surrey: the rules

items.t: Zoning (Bylaw No. 4662, 2010): RS2, RS3 and RS5 single-family zones, CD3 for Rodgers Creek (density set by lot size) and the Cypress Village (CV) zone. Secondary suites and detached secondary suites are allowed in the single-family zones and must be registered with the District.

Hazard permits: the main one here is a wildfire development permit for work within about 100 metres of undisturbed forest, since the area is steep and forested; an environmental development permit is needed for work within 15 metres of the top of any creek bank (Cypress Creek and Rodgers Creek both run through the area); and a foreshore permit applies to waterfront property at risk of coastal flooding.

If a parcel is in the ALR: subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified. On ALR land the main house can be up to 500 m², a suite is allowed only inside it, and an extra residence can be up to 90 m² (186 m² on parcels over 40 ha). For farm class, BC Assessment looks for farm income of $10,000 a year on under 0.8 ha, $2,500 on 0.8 to 4 ha, and $2,500 plus 5% of the value of land over 4 ha; applications are due by October 31.

blocks.text: Good to know about Cypress Park Estates lots

items.t: The Upper Lands growth is zoned, not rumoured: Cypress Village has its own CV Zone created by Zoning Amendment Bylaw No. 5206, 2024, and its first works are a numbered District permit (DP 24-115) — a seller's "village coming" claim can be checked against the District's development-applications page, permit by permit.

Three District parks sit inside the residential area: Cypress Falls Park, Cypress Trails Park and Woodburn Park are District parks here — distinct from the provincial park up the road that shares the Cypress name, a confusion the District's own Parks Master Plan listings keep separate (RS2/Dedicated; RS3/Dedicated).

The Guinness history is District record: the District history page states a British group led by the Guinness family purchased most of the Upper Lands above this area, began to build the British Properties, and built the Lions Gate Bridge — the development lineage behind the Rodgers Creek / Uplands parcels.

faq.a: It is the MLS site/area name for the Upper Lands pocket on Cypress Bowl Road, Chippendale Road and Uplands Way. District sources use Cypress Park, Rodgers Creek and the Uplands instead, and Cypress Village / Cypress West are the OCP's future neighbourhoods. It is not Cypress Mountain or the provincial park.
faq.q: Is Cypress Park Estates a real neighbourhood?

faq.a: One building: Hawksley on Uplands Way — freehold strata apartment/condo units (and 7 townhomes) by British Pacific Properties with Beedie Living, listed as built 2026. Everything else in the pocket is houses, semi-detached strata homes (Chippendale Mews), or unbuilt projects.
faq.q: What condos can I actually buy here today?

faq.a: The address is given as 3271–3281 Uplands Way in presale marketing and 3963 Uplands Way in current listings, and the size as 57 condos plus 7 townhomes or a "72-unit" building. Check the address, strata plan number and total units on the title and Form B or disclosure statement for a specific unit.
faq.q: Hawksley's address and unit count differ between sources — which do I trust?

faq.a: Listings state built 2026, so the building is complete; a unit still held by the developer is a new-home sale (5% GST, REDMA rescission on the original contract, Newly Built Home PTT Exemption may apply), while a unit resold by an owner is a resale (Form B route, no GST). Establish which seller you are dealing with first.
faq.q: Is a Hawksley purchase a presale or a resale, and does GST apply?

faq.a: Yes — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable anywhere in BC since November 24, 2022. Short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw; check the filed bylaws.
faq.q: Can I rent out a Hawksley condo long-term?

faq.a: Listings use the civic address 3963 Uplands Way (presale marketing used 3271–3281 Uplands Way) and classify the subdivision as Cypress Park Estates — it is Uplands/Rodgers Creek product above Highway 1.
faq.q: How many homes are in Hawksley, and where is it really?

faq.a: No. The residential area is in the District of West Vancouver on and below Cypress Bowl Road, while BC Parks states Cypress Mountain Resort is entirely within Cypress Park (Cypress Provincial Park), reached by Cypress Bowl Road from Highway 1.
faq.q: Is Cypress Park Estates the same place as Cypress Mountain?

faq.a: TransLink's 256 shuttle serves Chippendale Road at Westhill at the edge of the residential area and runs to Park Royal.
faq.q: Is there a bus to Cypress Mountain or to Park Royal?

faq.a: The District's Area Development Plan for Cypress Village and Eagleridge plans a new community west of Cypress Bowl Road with housing, employment space and community amenities; Council paired it with Zoning Amendment Bylaw No. 5206, 2024, initial works are under Development Permit 24-115 to British Pacific Properties Limited, and the Eagleridge lands transferred to the District were dedicated as park.
